inputs.description: Each scenario describes one institution or policy set and how DMV, DOT, and license data are used in access, mobility, or credit decisions affecting constitutional capital.

metrics.label: DMV-gated applicants (share)
metrics.description: Share of applicants whose access depends on DMV or license-status rules.

metrics.label: Noncommercial applicants affected
metrics.description: Estimated count of noncommercial applicants impacted by DMV-based or DOT-contaminated gatekeeping.

metrics.label: DOT / FMCSA misuse flag
metrics.description: Indicator for scenarios where DOT/FMCSA-style enforcement or MCSAP signals touch non-DOT-regulated populations.

metrics.label: No appeal / human review flag
metrics.description: Indicator for systems where denials based on DMV or license data cannot be meaningfully challenged.

metrics.label: CCRI System Integrity Index
metrics.description: 0–1 style index summarizing how independent the system is from DMV/DOT overreach and whether appeal safeguards exist.

data_integrity.description: How strictly the institution limits itself to lawful, relevant, and minimally intrusive data sources.

constitutional_alignment.description: Whether the rules respect federal supremacy, the right to travel, and limits on state police power.

access_fairness.description: Whether similarly situated applicants are treated alike without unlawful DMV/DOT-based discrimination.

economic_impact.description: Estimated effect on work access, income, and community-level productivity when barriers are in place.

narrative_templates.high_risk: This system shows severe dependency on unlawful DMV or DOT data for noncommercial access decisions. CCRI classifies it as HIGH DIVERGENCE and high constitutional capital suppression.
narrative_templates.moderate_risk: This system exhibits mixed practices. Some rules diverge from constitutional and federal boundaries. CCRI classifies it as MODERATE DIVERGENCE and a candidate for targeted correction.
narrative_templates.low_risk: This system relies primarily on lawful and relevant criteria. DMV and DOT contamination is low or absent. CCRI classifies it as LOW DIVERGENCE.

downstream_links.purpose: Convert CCRI divergence and population counts into recoverable economic value, mobility restoration, and work access.
Quantify financial and legal exposure where unlawful DMV or DOT signals are embedded in decision systems.
Translate CCRI corrections into budget categories for reinvestment.
Model long-term stability and recovery once the system is realigned.
